o: Merge all occupied intervals that overlap or touch (touching means next.start == current.end + 1), then delete every integer point inside [freeStart, freeEnd] from the merged result, returning what remains sorted and minimal. In Example 1, merging gives [2,8],[10,12],[14,16]; removing [7,11] splits the first into [2,6] and the second into [12,12]. In Example 2, [1,5] minus [3,8] leaves [1,2]. With up to 5e4 intervals and coordinates up to 1e9, sweeping point-by-point is impossible — we must work interval-interval.
k: Sorting by start lets a single linear pass merge overlapping/touching intervals.
Removing a free interval [fs, fe] from a merged [s, e] yields at most two pieces: [s, fs-1] and [fe+1, e], each kept only if non-empty.

a.i: Sort intervals by start. Sweep once, extending the current merged block while the next interval starts at or before current.end + 1 (the +1 implements 'touching'). Then, for each merged block, subtract the free interval by emitting up to two leftover pieces. Everything stays sorted because both the merge pass and clipping preserve order.
s: Merge passes: if s <= curEnd + 1, extend curEnd = max(curEnd, e); otherwise close the block and start a new one.
For each merged [s, e]: if it lies outside [freeStart, freeEnd], keep it whole; otherwise emit [s, freeStart-1] if s < freeStart and [freeEnd+1, e] if e > freeEnd.
a.t: O(k log k) time for sorting plus O(k) merging/clipping, where k is the number of intervals; O(k) space.
a.sp: O(k) — the merged list and the result.

w: This sort-and-sweep is the standard tool whenever coordinates reach 1e9 and forbid difference arrays. Pitfalls: forgetting that touching intervals merge (use s <= ce + 1, not s <= ce), and remembering ce + 1 can overflow 32-bit when ce = 1e9 (use 64-bit intermediates). Edge cases: the free interval covering everything (empty answer), or lying entirely outside all occupied blocks. Follow-up: support multiple free intervals — clip against each in sorted order, or merge frees first and sweep both lists with two pointers.
